title: Practice Test 1 · work standards and Little's Law
source: Exercises to practice, First Test (F. Martinez) and its answer key
intro:
Work standards in order:
  • Classify each activity: A unit, B batch, C shift time (some shift time is written outside the table).
  • NEED = unit time · units + batch time. HAVE = 480 − shift time.
  • Shifts = NEED / HAVE → full shifts + the minutes of the first day → count back from 17:00.

exercises.text: A batch of 120 pieces must be completed at the end of this Friday shift. Decide when it must start (day and shift; Monday = shift 1, one 8-hour shift a day starting at 9:00). Each shift uses 12 min for general cleaning of the shop floor at the end.

parts.model: Clamp 0.5 + turn 13.5 + release 0.5 + check 0.5 = 15 (type A: repeats for every piece).
Preparing 5 + cleaning the workplace 5 + general cleaning 12 (outside the table) = 22 (type C).

parts.q: b) Time to manufacture the batch, µ (min)
c) Time you HAVE per shift, µ (min)
c) Minutes still needed on the first day, µ

parts.model: The last 17 min of the day are cleaning (5 + 12). Count back 133 + 17 = 150 min from 17:00 → 14:30. With LTL ≈ 16:29, with UTL ≈ 12:31. The key assumes an activity can be split between days.

exercises.text: Little's Law. a) A coffee-shop queue has 10 people; one barista needs about 5 min per customer. b) A product waits 2 days in finished-goods inventory; the factory makes 10 finished goods per day. c) At peak a system processes 8 000 transactions per hour, average response time about 5 s, average think time per user about 30 s.

parts.q: a) Baristas needed to serve the 10 customers in 25 min
parts.model: One barista: 10 · 5 = 50 min. For 25 min you need half the time per customer (2.5 min) → 2 baristas.
